CheckTitle: Conditional Access policy restricts privileged roles to Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs)
Description:
An enabled Conditional Access policy should target **privileged directory roles**, apply to **all cloud apps**, **block access** from devices not matching a device filter that identifies **Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs)**.

This limits privileged sessions to hardened, dedicated devices and reduces the blast radius of a compromised endpoint.
Risk: Privileged users signing in from everyday workstations are exposed to **phishing**, **malware**, and **token theft**. Without restricting privileged sessions to dedicated PAWs, an attacker who compromises an ordinary endpoint can hijack admin credentials and escalate to **tenant-wide control**.

Code.Other:
1. Navigate to the Microsoft Entra admin center at https://entra.microsoft.com/
2. Go to **Protection** > **Conditional Access** > **Policies** > **New policy**
3. Under **Users**, select **Include** > **Select users and groups** > **Directory roles** and add each privileged role
4. Under **Target resources**, select **All cloud apps**
5. Under **Conditions** > **Filter for devices**, set mode to **Exclude** and add a rule matching PAWs (e.g., `device.extensionAttribute1 -eq "PAW"`)
6. Under **Grant**, select **Block access**
7. Exclude documented break-glass accounts under **Users** > **Exclude**
8. Test the policy in **Report-only** mode, then set to **On** and click **Save**

Recommendation.Text: Create a Conditional Access policy that **blocks** privileged role sign-ins from any device not identified as a **Privileged Access Workstation**. Use a device filter with an extension attribute or compliance tag to identify PAWs. Exclude only documented **break-glass accounts** and test in report-only mode before enforcing.

Notes: This check verifies that a device filter is present and configured, but cannot determine whether the filter rule accurately identifies PAWs. Manual review of the device filter rule is recommended.
